p01.why: A null pointer to member converts to false and a non-null one to true, so main returns 0.

p02.why: A pointer to void must not convert implicitly to another pointer type.

p03.why: nullptr and zero literals of any integer type convert to null pointers, and the program has no main.

p04.why: 1e300 converts to float as the largest finite value or infinity, and both exceed 3.0e38f; Clang and GCC give infinity in constant evaluation.

p05.why: Plain and Small promote to int, Big keeps unsigned long long, and char32_t promotes to unsigned int because int cannot hold all its values.

p06.why: A pointer to a member of a base converts implicitly to a pointer to the same member of a derived class.

p07.why: const is added at the inner level and also at every level above it, so the conversion is implicit.

p08.why: nullptr converts to bool only in direct initialization, and this is copy initialization.

p09.why: The conversion from int A::* to int D::* goes through the ambiguous base A.

p10.why: An integer variable with the value zero is not a null pointer constant.

p11.why: A zero literal in parentheses still counts as a null pointer constant.

p12.why: 1e10 does not fit in int, so the conversion is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p13.why: 1e10 to int is undefined at run time, and the float-cast-overflow sanitizer without recovery stops the program with a nonzero status; the spec only says undefined, and the sanitizer outcome comes from the test list.

p14.why: D has two B subobjects, so the derived-to-base conversion is ambiguous and not implicit.

p15.why: A NaN converts to true so main returns 0, but MUL-11 makes 0.0/0.0 undefined, so the spec does not settle this; the best guess is that x86-64 gives NaN.

p16.why: A nonzero integer must not convert to a pointer implicitly.

p17.why: Unary + turns the array into int* and the function name into a function pointer, and the program has no main.

p18.why: A character literal with value zero is not an integer literal, so it is not a null pointer constant (EDG accepts it, Q-0100).

p19.why: An unsigned bit-field of width 3 promotes to int, so 1 - 2 is -1, which is less than 0, and main returns 0.

p20.why: 0.1 rounds to one of the two nearest floats, both nonzero and below 0.11f.

p21.why: Nonzero gives true, 0.0, -0.0 and a null pointer give false, and a pointer of type int* (not nullptr itself) converts to bool in copy initialization.

p22.why: -0.5 drops its fraction to 0, which fits in unsigned, so the result is 0.

p23.why: bool, the char types, short, unsigned short and char16_t promote to int, wchar_t is smaller than long long on the target, and float keeps its type.

p24.why: Integer conversions keep the low bits: -1 gives ~0u, 300 gives 44, and -2 gives 65534.

p25.why: nullptr converts to bool in direct initialization with parentheses or braces.

p26.why: A noexcept function converts to a pointer to a function with or without noexcept.

p27.why: A pointer or reference to D converts implicitly to B, which is an unambiguous public base.

p28.why: A function without noexcept must not convert to a pointer to a noexcept function.

p29.why: const is added at the inner level without adding it at the level above.

p30.why: A pointer to a function must not convert to a pointer to void.

p31.why: A pointer to an array of known bound converts implicitly to a pointer to an array of unknown bound.

p32.why: const int* to void* removes a cv-qualifier.

p33.why: A pointer to a member of a derived class does not convert implicitly to a pointer to a member of the base.

p34.why: A pointer to a member function without noexcept must not convert to one with noexcept.

p35.why: Bit-fields promote by width: width 3 gives int, width 40 keeps long long, and unsigned width 32 promotes to unsigned int.

p36.why: Signed targets keep the low bits in two's complement: 200 gives -56, 4294967295u gives -1, and 40000 gives -25536.

p37.why: A zero literal converts to a null pointer to data member and to member function.

p38.why: Each value is between two adjacent floats, and the asserts accept either.

p39.why: The spec leaves the choice to the implementation, but every compiler in the matrix rounds to nearest with ties to even, which gives 16777220.0f.

p40.why: A pointer to a noexcept member function converts to one without noexcept.

p41.why: The literal false is not a null pointer constant.

p42.why: 2^24 fits exactly in float and 2^52 fits exactly in double.

p43.why: Object pointers convert to void pointers with the same or more cv-qualifiers.

p44.why: The member pointer conversion must not go through the virtual base B.

p45.why: Conversion drops the fraction toward zero: 3, -3 and 2.

p46.why: A null D* converts to a null B* even though B is at a nonzero offset, so main returns 0.

p47.why: -1.0 to unsigned is undefined, so constant evaluation rejects it.
